Needing at least three goals to stay in contention after suffering a 2-0 defeat in the first leg in Lubumbashi on Friday, Nigeria delivered an impressive performance to keep their hopes of reaching the continental tournament alive.
The Olympics Eagles wasted little time in setting the tone for the encounter, with Alex Oweilayefa opening the scoring just eight minutes after kick-off to give the hosts an early advantage.
The goal lifted the confidence of the Nigerian side, who continued to press for more goals in their bid to overturn the aggregate deficit.
Nigeria maintained their attacking momentum after the break and were rewarded in the 55th minute when Peter Edokpolor found the net to make it 2-0, drawing the aggregate score level at 2-2.
With the contest finely balanced, the 1996 Olympic football gold medallists pushed forward in search of the decisive goal and completed their comeback in the 63rd minute, scoring their third to take a 3-0 lead and move ahead 3-2 on aggregate before extending their advantage beyond DR Congo reach to 4-0 and 4-2 aggregate.
DR Congo could not find a response as Nigeria held on to their advantage until the final whistle, sparking celebrations among the home supporters.
The victory sends Nigeria into the final qualifying round, scheduled for March 2027, where they will battle for a place at the 2027 U-23 AFCON in Egypt.
The tournament will also serve as Africa’s qualification pathway for the men’s football event at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
For Nigeria, the comeback represents a significant boost after the disappointment of their first-leg defeat, keeping alive their ambition of returning to the Olympic football tournament.
The Olympics Eagles, who won gold at the Atlanta 1996 Games, will now turn their attention to the final hurdle in their quest to secure a place at the continental championship and move closer to another Olympic appearance.
